segments.text: Let's see the difference between the
same pad customization task done on
Alteium Designer 25 versus using a
previous version. The task involves
modifying a standard
QFN-32 5x5mm footprint to meet the
Renaissance FO480 package requirements.
Specifically, the pin pads need to be
rounded on the inner side only. The
solder mask expansion should be
increased by 0.05 mm while the paste
mask expansion should be reduced by 0.05
mm. For the thermal pad, a 0.3 mm
chamfer must be added to the top left
corner. Additionally, the pace mass
expansion must follow a window pattern
that provides 80% pace coverage with a
0.2 mm separation between openings. So,
let's get started. With the older
version of Alteium Designer on the
right, the engineer is doing a manual
execution method of required parameters
through the fill on each layer and
regions for window-shaped paste. For the
thermal pad, it requires measurement of
the reduction for the 80% cover and a
conversion of the lines into a region.
On the left, the engineers using the
built-in custom pad stack tool available
with Alteium Designer 25. Utilizing
Alteium Designer's built-in custom pad
stack tool took a mere 2 minutes and 5
seconds and only required 45 mouse
clicks. While the process without using
the custom pad stack tool took 6 minutes
and 2 seconds and requires 116 mouse
clicks, showing a clear advantage in
using Alteium Designer 25.

title: Take 66% of Your Time Back with Custom Pad Stack in Altium Designer 25
